# Capturefab

> A camera workbench with an iced desktop GUI, cross-platform CLI, local automation sessions, and one self-contained executable per platform.

## Canonical resources

- [Agent instructions](agents.md): CLI conventions, sessions, and acquisition workflow.
- [Workflow guide](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/cli-workflows.md): Repeatable JSON plans, paths, partial failures and PowerShell examples.
- [Workflow examples](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/tree/main/examples/workflows): Multi-camera timelapse, scanner feeder and bounded local recording.
- [Release manifest](releases.json): Versioned JSON with real published assets, architectures, SHA-256 checksums, and signatures when available. An empty releases array means no binaries are published.
- [Atom releases](feed.xml): Release announcements.
- [Source and build guide](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab): Source code, MIT license, CLI reference, and build instructions.
- [FFmpeg build notes](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/ffmpeg-build.md): Bundled media dependencies and source/build provenance.

## Start here

Run `capturefab schema --json` for the installed binary's automation contract, `capturefab doctor --json` for capabilities, and `capturefab sessions --json` to find an existing user session. Camera/session commands, discovery and network scans attach to the only authenticated active GUI/serve session. Multiple active sessions require `--session NAME`; no session falls back to temporary workers for supported camera operations. `--direct --camera ID` bypasses automatic attachment and overrides CAPTUREFAB_SESSION; it conflicts only with explicit --session. CAPTUREFAB_SESSION supplies a camera/session command default; CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA supplies the default source. --hwaccel configures new direct/GUI/serve workers; existing sessions keep their decoding setting.

Capturefab starts its GUI with no subcommand. Scripts should use explicit subcommands and `--json`. All JSON data commands, including schema, use {version:1,ok:true,result:...} or {version:1,ok:false,error:{code,message,...}}. Read schema's contract and dynamic CLI tree under result; plain schema prints the contract directly. Data goes to stdout and diagnostics go to stderr. Exit codes: 1 operation_failed, 2 usage, 3 unavailable, 4 timeout, 5 unsupported, 6 storage_full. --timeout-ms bounds each frame/transport operation; --request-timeout 5m bounds a session request. A timed-out command can still finish in the session: inspect status before retrying writes.

Inspection, feature writes, captures, recording, XML and memory commands connect a missing --camera source to the selected session. Desktop windows/browser tabs keep their own camera selection and drafts; select ID sets the session default for CLI calls without --camera. Humans and AI agents share cameras: same-camera commands run in order, independent cameras run concurrently, overlapping scheduled jobs share acquisition. Use --actor NAME --actor-kind agent (CAPTUREFAB_ACTOR/CAPTUREFAB_ACTOR_KIND) for recognizable agent attribution; human is the default kind. Activity immediately shows other actors, target cameras, queued/running/succeeded/failed states, errors and saved paths. status.result.activity and activity_revision include global history even for targeted busy-camera status. Entry.actor contains id/name/kind; entry.job tracks scheduled id/worker_pid/status/count/captured/last_file/error after acknowledgment. Last 200 completed entries plus active commands/jobs survive selection/disconnect. Read-only observations and probes do not add activity. Private local IPC: activity --json returns {revision,activity}; repeat activity --after REV --wait 20s --json for immediate changes without HTTP. RPC {op:activity,after:REV,timeout_ms:20000} is read-only and bypasses camera queues. HTTP GET /api/activity returns {revision,activity}; keep watching with ?after=REV&timeout_ms=20000 (max25000) for immediate command/job changes visible to every watcher. POST /api/command supports optional actor:{id,name,kind} display attribution, not authentication.

Journal strings/path previews are capped: captures retain first eight paths in files with file_count giving the actual total; command results still return the complete file list. Schedule previews advance with acquired frames. Targeted --camera ID status retains full coordinator context (cameras, devices, network_scan, logs, activity) with queried-camera fields at top level. target_camera identifies the canonical queried ID; active_camera retains the session default for untargeted CLI calls, independently of desktop/browser local selection.

Use workflow validate FILE --json, workflow apply FILE --dry-run --json, then --session NAME workflow apply FILE --json. Validation/dry-run are offline. Documents are {version:1,steps:[{camera?:ID,command:SessionCommand}]}, use the strict RPC command fields, reject unknown/duplicate fields, and permit 1–256 steps in at most 1 MiB. Connect/select use command.camera and omit the outer camera; discover/network_scan also omit it. All steps validate before execution; live device and destination checks remain. Apply requires a persistent session, uses each step's camera, rejects global --camera, and stops on first failure with prior effects intact. error.details.completed/completed_steps/failed_step describe partial execution. Jobs and encoders keep running in the session after apply exits; inspect jobs/status before retrying.

Raw logs keep time/level/message and may add timestamp:{unix_ms,utc_offset_seconds}. unix_ms is signed Unix milliseconds for the absolute event; utc_offset_seconds is the producer clock's offset east of UTC (-86399..86399). Legacy time has no date/zone: do not parse it as an instant. Missing/malformed optional metadata remains unknown without hiding the diagnostic. Desktop/browser render valid instants in the viewer's local zone; copied desktop logs include a dated numeric offset. This is an additive version-1 output field; existing fields/envelopes remain unchanged.

CLI/RPC local sources and outputs use the caller directory; workflow sources/outputs use the file's directory (stdin uses caller directory). file:relative.mkv and sim:replay:relative-folder sources resolve in connect/select and outer camera targets; bare existing filenames are file sources. Prefer file: for local-source names that could also be camera IDs. Network/device locators, stream URLs and destination-relative names stay unchanged. Workflow captures cannot write binary stdout. Single capture/template extensions infer png/jpeg/raw/pgm/ppm; directory sequences default png; --format overrides. record/forward --duration 30s works for temporary workers and sessions, keeps the CLI alive and stops the encoder at deadline or Ctrl-C. Without duration, sessions return immediately and need stop-forward; direct commands run until Ctrl-C. Workflow protocol has no duration/wait field: use separate start/stop files or timed CLI recording. PowerShell can pass workflow files directly or Get-Content -Raw workflow.json | capturefab workflow validate - --json.

Persistent camera sessions expose `history`, `undo` and `redo`: use `--session NAME [--camera ID] history --json` for the next labels. GUI, CLI and RPC reversible camera changes share this bounded per-camera history, which lasts for the connection. Replay detects conflicts and retains failed entries. Captures, uploads, recordings, schedules, connection changes, arbitrary commands and raw memory writes are outside camera history; stopping with active schedules or forwarding is also excluded. The desktop uses ⌘Z/⇧⌘Z on macOS and Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z (also Ctrl+Y redo) elsewhere.
Scanner settings are reversible. Scanner acquisition, including Start and Stop, may move or consume physical pages and cannot be undone or replayed.

Use `capturefab --session NAME network-scan --json` to inspect IPv4 adapters, rediscover/probe GigE cameras and tune connected cameras within a shared per-interface budget. RPC is `{"op":"network_scan","timeout_ms":1000}`; result/status.network_scan contains interfaces, cameras, warnings and scanned_at_ms. Health values: unreachable, limited, unverified, ready, unstable. Discovery does not prove reachability or stability. The scan briefly pauses previews to retest packet sizes, uses supported camera throughput/pacing controls, and keeps auto within the budget; active recordings, forwarding and schedules skip tuning with guidance. It does not change host IPs, routes or MTUs. Per-camera `{"op":"optimize_network","bytes_per_second":100000000}` applies a supplied budget; prefer the session scan for shared-link accounting. Network defaults are outside undo history.

Captures, schedules and recordings accept `--destination NAME` for a saved folder (including external and network drives) or S3-compatible bucket; `capturefab destination list --json`, `volumes --json` and `uploads --json` describe them and the upload queue. Credentials stay in the OS credential store or standard AWS sources. Use `capturefab storage --json` to inspect the saved global storage ceiling and live reservations. Captures and local video recordings share that budget across processes using the same session directory. A storage-full failure has exit code 6. Retention deletion and raising a global budget require explicit user authorization.

Auto mode is opt-in per camera: `capturefab --session NAME auto [--balance 0..1]` (0 favors image quality, 1 frame rate) and `manual [--revert]`. `status --json` reports `auto` (null in manual mode) with its recent changes. Ask before enabling it on cameras other software uses.

CameraInfo includes `profile: {kind, source, evidence, capabilities}` in discovery devices, info.camera and status.connected/status.cameras[].info. Kinds: unknown, area_scan, line_scan, depth, microscope, thermal, document_scanner. Sources: unknown, transport, identity, features, device_metadata. Evidence is a string array; capabilities lists advertised control families, not guaranteed writable controls. Discovery can be provisional; connection refines metadata from readable features. Detection prioritizes scanner transport, explicit device class metadata, explicit Linescan geometry, specialty features, remaining scan geometry, model identity, then image dimensions/frame timing. A one-row ROI, high bit depth or vendor name alone is not type evidence. Inspect features and selector-dependent limits; see schema --json's result.camera_profiles.

The GUI prioritizes line geometry/timing and triggers/encoders, depth components/range/calibration, microscope optics/illumination/stage, thermal temperature/calibration, or scanner controls. Microscope previews retain focus and sharpness tools. Line history shows recent received display rows with gaps for skipped blocks and may downsample; captures save individual blocks, not a complete reconstructed scan. Scalar depth/thermal previews color an automatic raw-value range without applying device calibration; Sensor pixels returns to the ordinary preview. For quantitative samples use capture --format raw and retain device component, unit, scale, offset and calibration features separately. Raw preserves bytes and precision; PNG/JPEG/PGM/PPM and forwarded video are 8-bit visualizations; forwarding carries no GUI color map or measurement calibration. Transports acquire single rasters; depth must provide a compatible single-component stream. Multipart, GenDC, point-cloud payloads and vendor SDK-only depth access remain unsupported. Detection implies no physical camera compatibility. Generic auto exposure is unsupported for line scan, depth, thermal and document scanner sources; image cameras including microscopes retain support when suitable controls are advertised.

Typed synthetic sources are sim:line[:name], sim:depth[:name], sim:microscope[:name] and sim:thermal[:name]; sim:0 and arbitrary other names remain area scan. Examples: `capturefab --camera sim:line capture --set Height=1 --set AcquisitionLineRate=2000 --set ExposureTime=100 -o line.png`; `capturefab --camera sim:depth capture --format raw -o depth.raw`; `capturefab --camera sim:microscope capture --set FocusPosition=50 --set Magnification=4 --set IlluminationIntensity=70 -o micrograph.png`; `capturefab --camera sim:thermal get TemperatureLinearResolution TemperatureUnit --json` and `capturefab --camera sim:thermal capture --format raw -o thermal.raw`. Synthetic sources exercise controls and transport behavior, not hardware compatibility.

Release data is authoritative for available downloads. Select the target matching the installed operating system and architecture. Do not infer Apple Silicon versus Intel from a Macintosh browser user-agent string.

Document scanners are listed by `scanners --json` and included in `discover` with transport `scanner`. Select the full `scanner:sane:DEVICE`, `scanner:wia:ID`, or `scanner:ica:UUID` ID. Linux needs SANE scanimage/backends, Windows uses WIA drivers and Windows PowerShell, and macOS uses a bundled ImageCaptureCore helper. The default `scanner` feature and runtime availability appear in `doctor`. Use `--timeout-ms 60000 capture -o document.png`; set ScanResolution (75–600 dpi, default 150), ScanMode (Color/Gray/Lineart) and ScanSource (Default/Flatbed/Feeder) with capture --set. Each capture requests one page and count saves successive pages as separate images; connecting/start never scans. GUI scanner timeout defaults to 60 seconds. Driver support varies and has not been physically validated. Existing capture image formats, schedules, destinations and quotas apply; no PDF/OCR, scanner forwarding or auto exposure. Samples normalize to 8-bit RGB/grayscale with a 128 MiB page bound.
